chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from the one who narrated to him, from Yazid ibn Khalifah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That he disliked prayer in the garment saturated with safflower, dyed with safron.

key_terms.الْعُصْفُرِ: Safflower (a plant used for yellow dye)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in clothes dyed with saffron or safflower?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expressed dislike (karahah) for praying in garments heavily saturated with safflower and dyed with saffron, a ruling rooted in the potential for the strong, distinct scent to distract the worshipper during recitation. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the principle that while such materials are not inherently impure, excessive sensory stimulation from strong perfumes or dyes can detract from the khushu (focus) required for valid prayer.
